p.src: Now Yang’s chief general proposed a plan to attack Liu Bei. Yuan Shu asked, “What is your plan?” The general replied, “Liu Bei’s army is stationed at Xiaopei and would be easy enough to defeat, but Lü Bu holds Xuzhou like a crouching tiger. We promised him gold, silk, grain, and horses before, yet have given him nothing to this day, so I fear he may aid Liu Bei. We should now send him provisions to win his goodwill and induce him to keep his troops still; then Liu Bei can be captured. Capture Liu Bei first and deal with Lü Bu afterward, and Xuzhou will be ours.” Yuan Shu was delighted. He prepared two hundred thousand hu of millet and ordered Han Yin to carry a secret letter to Lü Bu. Lü Bu was greatly pleased and treated Han Yin with high honor. Han Yin returned and reported to Yuan Shu, who then appointed Ji Ling commander-in-chief, with Lei Bo and Chen Lan as his deputies, and sent them with tens of thousands of troops to attack Xiaopei.

p.src: Meanwhile, Ji Ling advanced swiftly with his army, reached the southeast of Pei County, and pitched camp. By day, ranks of banners screened the mountains and rivers; by night, signal fires blazed and drums thundered as though shaking heaven and earth apart. Xuande had only a little over five thousand men in the town, yet was forced to lead them out, form ranks, and establish a camp. Suddenly word came that Lü Bu had led his army to a point one li from the town and encamped to the southwest. Learning that Lü Bu had come with troops to rescue Liu Bei, Ji Ling hastily sent him a letter reproaching him for breaking faith. Lü Bu laughed. “I have a plan that will leave neither the Yuan nor the Liu house bearing me a grudge.” He sent messengers to the camps of Ji Ling and Liu Bei, inviting both men to a banquet.

p.src: Xuande did not know what Lü Bu intended and felt uneasy. Ji Ling dismounted and entered the camp, but when he saw Xuande seated in the command tent, he was greatly startled and turned at once to leave. The attendants could not detain him. Lü Bu stepped forward and hauled him back with one hand as easily as lifting a child. Ji Ling said, “Does the general mean to kill me?” Lü Bu replied, “No.” Ji Ling asked, “Then do you mean to kill the big-eared fellow?” Lü Bu replied, “Not that either.” Ji Ling asked, “Then what is this about?” Lü Bu said, “Xuande and I are brothers. Since he is now hard-pressed by you, General, I have come to rescue him.” Ji Ling said, “If so, does that mean you will kill me?” Lü Bu replied, “There is no such reason. All my life I have disliked fighting and cared only to stop fights. Today I shall settle the quarrel between your two houses.” Ji Ling said, “May I ask how you intend to settle it today?” Lü Bu replied, “I have a way to let Heaven decide.” He pulled Ji Ling into the tent and brought him face-to-face with Xuande. Each man regarded the other with suspicion. Lü Bu seated himself between them, placing Ji Ling on his left and Liu Bei on his right, then ordered a banquet prepared and wine served.

p.src: After several rounds of wine, Lü Bu said, “For my sake, let both your houses withdraw their troops.” Xuande said nothing. Ji Ling said, “By my lord’s command, I have brought one hundred thousand troops expressly to seize Liu Bei. How can I withdraw?” Zhang Fei flew into a rage, drew his sword, and shouted, “Though my troops are few, I regard the likes of you as mere child’s play! How do you compare with the million Yellow Turbans? You dare harm my elder brother!” Lord Guan hastily restrained him, saying, “Let us first see what General Lü intends. We can always return to our camps and fight afterward.” Lü Bu said, “I invited both houses here to stop your quarrel. I will not have you fighting.”

p.src: Ji Ling seethed with resentment on one side, while Zhang Fei on the other was bent on fighting. Lü Bu grew furious and ordered, “Attendants! Bring me my halberd!” Lü Bu took his painted halberd in hand. Ji Ling and Xuande both turned pale. Lü Bu said, “Whether you two houses cease fighting shall be left entirely to Heaven’s will.” He ordered his attendants to take the painted halberd and plant it far outside the camp gate. Then he turned to Ji Ling and Xuande and said, “The camp gate is one hundred and fifty paces from the command tent. If I strike the small side blade of the halberd with a single arrow, both your houses must withdraw their troops; if I miss, each of you may return to camp and prepare for battle. If either refuses to obey me, the other and I shall combine our strength against him.” Ji Ling thought privately, “The halberd stands one hundred and fifty paces away. How could he possibly hit it? I may as well agree. When he misses, I can fight as I please.” He promptly gave his word. Xuande naturally had no objection. Lü Bu had them both sit again and drink another cup of wine.

p.src: We shall say no more of Xuande’s return to Xiaopei or Lü Bu’s return to Xuzhou. Meanwhile, Ji Ling returned to Huainan and met Yuan Shu. He related how Lü Bu had reconciled the two sides by shooting at the halberd outside the camp gate, and presented Lü Bu’s letter. Yuan Shu flew into a rage. “Lü Bu accepted so much grain from me, yet now he favors Liu Bei through this childish game! I shall personally lead a great army to campaign against Liu Bei and punish Lü Bu as well!” Ji Ling said, “My lord, you must not act rashly. Lü Bu possesses strength and valor beyond other men, and he also holds the territory of Xuzhou. If he and Liu Bei support each other from front and rear, they will not be easy to overcome. I have heard that Lü Bu’s wife, Lady Yan, has a daughter who has reached marriageable age. Since my lord has a son, you could send someone to seek a marriage alliance with Lü Bu. If Lü Bu gives his daughter in marriage to your son, he will surely kill Liu Bei. This is the stratagem of preventing distant ties from coming between close kin.”

p.src: Yuan Shu followed his advice and that very day sent Han Yin as matchmaker, bearing gifts to Xuzhou to propose the marriage. When Han Yin reached Xuzhou and met Lü Bu, he declared, “My lord has long admired you, General, and wishes to take your esteemed daughter as his son’s wife, that our two houses may be forever joined in marriage.” Lü Bu went inside to consult his wife, Lady Yan. As it happened, Lü Bu had two wives and one concubine: he had first married Lady Yan as his principal wife, and later taken Diaochan as a concubine; while living in Xiaopei, he had also married Cao Bao’s daughter as his second wife. Lady Cao had died before him without issue, and Diaochan likewise had borne no children; only Lady Yan had given birth to a daughter, whom Lü Bu cherished above all.

p.src: Lady Yan then said to Lü Bu, “I have heard that Yuan Gonglu has long held Huainan, with abundant troops and provisions, and sooner or later will become emperor. If he accomplishes that great enterprise, our daughter may hope to become empress or imperial consort. I only wonder how many sons he has?” Lü Bu replied, “Only one.” His wife said, “If so, you should accept at once. Even if she does not become empress, our Xuzhou will be free from anxiety.” Lü Bu’s mind was thus made up. He treated Han Yin with lavish courtesy and consented to the match. Han Yin returned and reported to Yuan Shu. Yuan Shu immediately prepared the betrothal gifts and again ordered Han Yin to deliver them to Xuzhou. Lü Bu accepted them, gave a banquet in Han Yin’s honor, and lodged him at the posthouse to rest.

p.src: The next day, Chen Gong went directly to the posthouse to pay his respects to Han Yin. After exchanging courtesies, they sat down. Chen Gong dismissed the attendants and said to Han Yin, “Who proposed this scheme? Was the purpose of arranging a marriage between Lord Yuan and Fengxian to take Liu Xuande’s head?” Han Yin started in alarm, rose, and pleaded, “I beg you, Gongtai, do not reveal it!” Chen Gong said, “I shall not reveal it. I only fear that if the matter is delayed, someone else will see through it and unforeseen changes will thwart the plan.” Han Yin said, “Then what are we to do? I pray you instruct me.” Chen Gong said, “I shall see Fengxian and have him send his daughter to complete the match this very day. What say you?” Han Yin was delighted and thanked him, saying, “If you do so, Lord Yuan will be deeply grateful for your illustrious kindness!”

p.src: Chen Gong said, “At present, the lords of the realm contend with one another for supremacy. Now that you are forming a marriage alliance with Yuan Gonglu, can you be certain none of the other lords will be jealous? If you choose some distant auspicious date, one of them may seize the opportune moment to lay an ambush along the road and abduct her. What would you do then? As matters stand, if you mean to refuse the match, that is the end of it; but since you have accepted, you should send your daughter to Shouchun at once, before the other lords learn of it, and have her reside in a separate mansion there until an auspicious day is chosen for the wedding. Then nothing can go wrong.” Lü Bu said with delight, “Gongtai’s words are most sound.” He then went inside and told Lady Yan. That very night they prepared the bridal trousseau and made ready fine horses and a perfumed carriage. Lü Bu ordered Song Xian and Wei Xu to accompany Han Yin in escorting his daughter. With drums and music resounding to the heavens, the procession escorted her beyond the city.

p.src: Lü Bu was greatly alarmed and cried, “Chen Gong has misled me!” He urgently ordered Zhang Liao to lead troops in pursuit. Yu Jin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, led the troops under his own command against them along the road, killing the marauders and reassuring the villagers.
The Qingzhou troops fled back, prostrated themselves weeping before Cao Cao, and claimed that Yu Jin had rebelled and was pursuing and killing the Qingzhou forces.
Cao Cao was greatly alarmed.
Before long, Xiahou Dun, Xu Chu, Li Dian, and Yue Jin all arrived.
Cao Cao said that Yu Jin had rebelled and ordered the troops made ready to meet him.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Yu Jin saw that Cao Cao and the others had all arrived, he deployed his troops to secure the flanks of the formation with archery, then dug a trench and established a camp.

u.src: Meanwhile, when Yu Jin saw that Cao Cao and the others had all arrived, he deployed his troops to secure the flanks of the formation with archery, then dug a trench and established a camp.

p.src: Someone reported this to him, saying, “The Qingzhou troops say that you have rebelled. Now that the Chancellor has arrived, why do you not explain yourself instead of first fortifying a camp?” Yu Jin replied, “The enemy pursuers are behind us and may arrive at any moment. If we do not prepare first, how can we withstand them? Explaining myself is a small matter; repelling the enemy is the great one.” Just as the camp was completed, Zhang Xiu's forces attacked along two routes. Yu Jin personally led the way out of the camp to meet the enemy. Zhang Xiu hastily withdrew his troops. Seeing Yu Jin advance, the officers on either side each led their troops into the attack. Zhang Xiu's army suffered a crushing defeat and was pursued and slaughtered for more than a hundred li. His strength exhausted and his position isolated, Zhang Xiu led his defeated troops away to seek refuge with Liu Biao.

p.src: Cao Cao recalled his army and mustered his officers. Yu Jin came before him and explained in full that the Qingzhou troops had wantonly plundered, gravely alienating the people, and that this was why he had killed them. Cao Cao said, “Why did you establish a camp before reporting to me?” Yu Jin answered as he had before. Cao Cao said, “Amid such turmoil, General, you were able to order the troops and fortify the defenses, bearing both slander and hardship, and turn defeat into victory. Even the renowned generals of old could not have surpassed this!” He then bestowed upon Yu Jin a set of gold vessels and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yishou Village. He reproved Xiahou Dun for his failure to discipline his troops strictly. He also held a sacrifice for Dian Wei. Cao Cao himself wept and poured a libation for him, then turned to his officers and said, “I lost my eldest son and my beloved nephew, yet I feel no such profound grief for either. For Dian Wei alone do I wail and shed tears.” All present were moved and sighed. The next day, he ordered the army to return.

p.src: We shall say no more of Cao Cao's return to the capital at Xu. Instead, Wang Ze bore the imperial edict to Xuzhou. Lü Bu welcomed him into the residence, where the edict was opened and read: Lü Bu was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and specially granted the seals and ribbons of office. Wang Ze also produced Cao Cao's private letter. Before Lü Bu, Wang Ze spoke at length of Lord Cao's regard and respect for him. Lü Bu was delighted. Suddenly, word came that Yuan Shu had sent an envoy. Lü Bu summoned the man and questioned him. The envoy said, “Lord Yuan will ascend the imperial throne at any moment and establish the Eastern Palace. He urges that the imperial bride be brought to Huainan without delay.” Lü Bu flew into a rage. “How dare that traitor act so!” he cried. He immediately killed the envoy, locked Han Yin in a cangue, and sent Chen Deng bearing a memorial of thanks to escort Han Yin together with Wang Ze to the capital at Xu and express gratitude for the imperial favor. He also sent Cao Cao a reply requesting formal appointment as Governor of Xuzhou.

p.src: When Cao Cao learned that Lü Bu had broken off the marriage alliance with Yuan Shu, he was overjoyed and had Han Yin beheaded in the marketplace. Chen Deng secretly advised Cao Cao, “Lü Bu is a jackal and a wolf. He is brave but devoid of strategy and changes allegiance lightly. You should deal with him soon.” Cao Cao said, “I have long known that Lü Bu harbors the wild ambition of a wolf cub. Truly, he cannot be kept for long. No one but you and your father can fathom his true disposition. You must help me devise a plan against him.” Chen Deng replied, “If the Chancellor takes action, I shall respond from within.” Cao Cao was delighted. He memorialized the throne to grant Chen Gui the post of Administrator, with a salary of two thousand piculs, and appointed Chen Deng Administrator of Guangling. As Chen Deng took his leave to return, Cao Cao held his hand and said, “I entrust the affairs of the east to you.”

p.src: Chen Deng nodded his assent and returned to Xuzhou to see Lü Bu. When Lü Bu questioned him, Chen Deng said that his father had been granted a salaried office and that he himself had been made an administrator. Lü Bu flew into a rage and said, “You did not seek the governorship of Xuzhou for me but instead sought rank and emolument for yourself! Your father advised me to join with Lord Cao and break off the marriage with Gonglu. Now I have gained nothing I sought, while you and your father have both risen to honor. I have been sold out by the pair of you!” He drew his sword and made to behead Chen Deng. Chen Deng laughed loudly. “General, how can you be so utterly blind?” he said. Lü Bu said, “How am I blind?” Chen Deng replied, “When I saw Lord Cao, I told him that keeping you, General, was like keeping a tiger: one must feed it its fill of meat. If it is not satisfied, it will devour men.” Lord Cao laughed and said, “That is not the way of it. I treat the Marquis of Wen like a hunting hawk. While foxes and hares remain, I dare not let it eat its fill too soon. When hungry it serves my purpose; once full, it will soar away.” I asked, “Who are the foxes and hares?” Lord Cao replied, “Yuan Shu in Huainan, Sun Ce east of the Yangtze, Yuan Shao in Jizhou, Liu Biao in Jingzhou, Liu Zhang in Yizhou, and Zhang Lu in Hanzhong—they are all foxes and hares.” Lü Bu flung down his sword and laughed. “Lord Cao understands me!” he exclaimed. While they were still speaking, a sudden report came that Yuan Shu's army was advancing to seize Xuzhou. Lü Bu was startled when he heard the news. Indeed:
